one_line: Film a calm, fixed-camera montage in soft window light where the product is used in every shot.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 top-down on a toddler climbing foam steps, seen from behind, in striped window sun. No speech. The only text is a white script "Bliss" mark centred over the child from 0:00 to 0:02.
q1_hook.why: Motion and the product in use from frame one (H1, S1, E1). But nothing is said or promised: no question, no benefit, no Hebrew, only a brand mark (H2, T3, H6). The centred mark held over the child for about 2 s is the plastered kind of branding (H3).

beats.what: Top-down: toddler climbs the foam steps; script "Bliss" mark
beats.why: Product in use at once, in pretty light

beats.what: Wide living room shot of the play set, then a close-up of the cube's round hole
beats.why: Shows the set and its material

beats.what: Toddler crawls through the round hole; "Little steps, big moments" types in
beats.why: The only line of text, a feeling in English

beats.what: Static view of the cube and the slide ramp, a brown pouf beside
beats.why: Shows the full set in a styled room

beats.what: Toddler pushes soft blocks near the set and the slide ramp
beats.why: A new kind of play in each shot

beats.what: Toddler crawls toward the slide ramp
Top-down: she crawls out of the hole and away; a name tag and the mark appear

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None. No question, save or share ask in the video or the caption.
q2_flow.why: A new angle or activity every 2 to 3 s keeps a quiet montage moving (R3, E2). With nothing said and no stakes, nothing pulls the viewer to the end (K2). The last shot holds one crawl for almost 6 s (R1), though 24 s suits a single-mood piece (R2).

q3_cta.what: None. The video has no Hebrew text at all. The caption ends on a personal line about watching the child discover new ways to play, with no link, price, tag or ask.
q3_cta.why: A viewer who likes the set is not told what to do or where to buy (C6). With no ask there is no bait (C1, C2), but also no reason to send or comment, though a baby discovering a play set is a moment a grandparent might send (C4, R5).

q4_shown.what: A toddler climbing, crawling through and pushing blocks on a beige foam play set; the set in wide shots in a tidy white living room at 0:03 and 0:09. No adult, hands, price or product text. Benefits appear only in the caption.
q4_shown.why: Real use shows what the pieces do (S1, F8), and the wide shots let a parent picture it at home. The caption's "stable" and "wipes clean" are never shown, and no principle in the list covers that. A name tag at 0:23 names the child (S5).

q5_edit.what: About 10 shots in 24 s (first pass cut times), about 2.4 s each, straight cuts, fixed camera in most. No speed changes seen. One typed-in English tagline. Ends on a name tag overlay on the crawl, no end card.
q5_edit.why: Calm fixed shots every 2 to 3 s suit a mood montage (E2, R3). With no voice and no Hebrew text the message is only visual (E4). The ending repeats the opening top-down climb, a soft loop (R4).

q6_topic.what: A quiet, aesthetic montage of a toddler exploring a foam play set at home; it serves parents who want a play piece that also looks good.
q6_topic.why: The mood is tender and calm, mild next to the high-arousal feelings that travel (K1). It names no parent worry or moment (K6, K7), and the child's face is mostly hidden, so there is no reaction peak (K8).

q7_filmed.what: Fixed phone shots in soft window light with striped sun: top-down on the toddler, eye-level and low angles on the set, one close-up of the cube's hole. Neutral beige and white room, no adult, child filmed mostly from behind or above.
q7_filmed.why: Soft light, steady frames and a tidy room look clean on a phone (E6, F7), and live footage of the product in use fills the runtime (F8). It looks styled and brand-like, less like a parent's quick clip (H8). The set is small in the wide shots (F4).

q8_text.on_screen: English only: a white script "Bliss" mark centred over the child 0:00 to 0:02; "Little steps, big moments" typed in white handwriting on the foam at 0:06 to 0:08; at 0:23 a name tag with the child's name and the mark. No Hebrew on screen.
q8_text.caption: "הגימבורי של בליס ☁️הרבה מעבר למשחק." About 33 words: minimalist design, development, stable, wipes clean, a personal line with the child's name. No hashtags, no CTA, no disclosure.
q8_text.why: The caption carries the product name and four benefits in Hebrew, a good first line (T7), but the video has no Hebrew, so a muted viewer gets a mood and no message (T1, T3). The brand mark appears twice, first centred (H3). No hashtags and no disclosure (T7, T8).

weak_points: No Hebrew on screen and no spoken line; benefits only in the caption; no CTA; a six-second final shot of one crawl; the child's name on a name tag; a brand mark centred over the child at the start.
lumebook_takeaway: Film hands turning pages of a book in soft window light, phone fixed, one page or cover per shot, with one Hebrew line on screen saying why.
not_verified: Music (not established; the transcript is "תודה רבה" only); the toddler's age and relation to the creator; whether the Reel was paid (coauthor bliss.il, no label). Correction to src/coded: the first-frame text is the "Bliss" mark only; the child is seen from behind or above, so no face is on camera.
